claim_text: ISR requires an approved signature or recipient authorization. OP-117 recognizes an in-person signature at the delivery address, a signed indirect delivery to another address, an eligible recipient-signed Shipment Status Door Tag, a paper Shipment Release Authorization, or an electronic signature received through FedEx Delivery Manager. Each path has different documentation requirements.
allocation_basis: OP-117 page 12 identifies the primary ISR sources; pages 20, 22, 23, and 25 establish the indirect, signed-tag, SRA, and online-signature branches.

claim_text: First confirm FORGE shows ISR and no stricter service applies. Use one approved path: an in-person signature at the address; a signed indirect delivery to a neighbor with the address and door tag recorded; an eligible signed door tag; an applicable paper SRA; or an Electronic Signature Received in FORGE. If none applies, do not leave the package—apply the appropriate attempt status, complete and scan the door tag, and capture the prompted attempt photo.
allocation_basis: These pages establish each summarized approved path and the status, door-tag, PPODA, and do-not-leave response when none can be completed.

claim_text: For indirect delivery, record the actual alternate address, obtain the signature there, and complete/scan a door tag naming the location for the original primary entrance. A recipient-signed tag requires ALT, the recipient name, a clear tag-signature image, and return of the full tag. Paper SRA forms have separate barcoded and non-barcoded workflows and must be turned in. An online signature is recognized when FORGE receives the intercept and replaces the ISR icon.
allocation_basis: OP-117 provides the branch-specific address, signature, image, and form-return requirements; FORGE pages 73-76 corroborate the indirect-delivery UI sequence.

claim_text: Package is identified in FORGE as Indirect Signature Required
allocation_basis: OP-117 page 12 says signature-service packages are identified in FORGE and defines the ISR branch.

claim_text: For indirect delivery, someone at the alternate address must accept and sign; the actual indirect address and recipient notification must be recorded
allocation_basis: OP-117 pages 20 and 46 require the neighboring-location signature, actual indirect address, and door-tag notice; FORGE pages 73-76 show the address/tag prompts.

claim_text: For recipient-signed door-tag release, the package must not be DSR, ASR, or Appointment Delivery, the release location must be safe, and the signed-tag capture and return steps apply
allocation_basis: OP-117 page 22 states the signed-tag service exclusions, safe-location condition, ALT/name/photo steps, and return of the full tag.

claim_text: Paper SRA processing differs for barcoded and non-barcoded forms; an electronic signature is usable only when FORGE receives the on-road intercept and replaces the ISR icon
allocation_basis: OP-117 pages 23-25 distinguish barcoded and non-barcoded SRA processing and define the electronic-signature intercept/icon condition.

claim_text: ISR alternatives do not override stricter DSR, ASR, alcohol/controlled-substance, or Appointment Delivery requirements
allocation_basis: OP-117 and OP-119 distinguish ISR alternatives from stricter DSR, ASR, alcohol, and Appointment requirements; the wording preserves those overrides rather than extending ISR authorization.

claim_text: Path-specific signature or recipient authorization associated with the package in FORGE
allocation_basis: The ISR paths on these pages each associate the applicable in-person, indirect, signed-tag, SRA, or electronic authorization with the delivery workflow.

claim_text: Actual indirect-delivery address, signer signature, and completed/scanned OP-200 left at the original primary entrance when using an indirect location
allocation_basis: The cited pages require the actual indirect address, neighboring signature, and completed/scanned door tag at the original address.

claim_text: Recipient first initial and last name, signed-tag image, and physical signed tag returned to the station when using recipient-signed door-tag release
allocation_basis: OP-117 page 22 expressly requires recipient name, a close signed-tag image, and return of the entire signed tag.

claim_text: Applicable barcoded or non-barcoded SRA processing and physical-form check-in when using a paper SRA
allocation_basis: OP-117 pages 23-25 define the two paper-SRA scanner paths and require physical SRA check-in, plus the door tag for the non-barcoded path.

claim_text: Do not leave an ISR package through ordinary unattended driver release without one of the approved signature or recipient-authorization paths
allocation_basis: ISR requires one of the specified signature/authorization methods; OP-119 also says signature-service packages are not ordinary driver-release packages.

claim_text: Do not use an indirect location without the required alternate-address signature and recipient door-tag notification
allocation_basis: The indirect-delivery sources require an alternate-address signature, recorded address, and door-tag notification, excluding unsigned neighbor drop-off.

claim_text: If no approved ISR path can be completed, apply the appropriate unsuccessful-attempt status, complete and scan the door tag, capture PPODA when prompted, do not leave the package, and retain it for the applicable station-return or reattempt process
allocation_basis: The sources establish the unsuccessful status, completed/scanned tag, prompted PPODA, do-not-leave requirement, station return where delivery cannot be completed, and the applicable later-attempt/QA framework.

claim_text: Does FORGE identify the package as ISR, and is any stricter service also present?
allocation_basis: Signature-service identity and stricter overlapping services determine whether the ISR alternatives are available.

claim_text: Is someone available at the labeled address to sign?
allocation_basis: Both sources make an in-person signer at the delivery address one complete ISR path.

claim_text: Is a neighboring recipient available to accept and sign?
allocation_basis: Neighbor availability and willingness to sign determine whether the indirect-delivery branch can be completed.

claim_text: Is there an eligible signed door tag, paper SRA, or Electronic Signature Received icon?
allocation_basis: These pages define the signed-tag, paper-SRA, and Electronic Signature Received alternatives and their different processing.

claim_text: Confirm FORGE identifies ISR and check whether another service restriction requires the stricter DSR, ASR, alcohol/controlled-substance, or Appointment Delivery branch.
allocation_basis: The sources require identifying ISR and preserving stricter DSR, ASR, alcohol, and Appointment restrictions before selecting a release path.

claim_text: Use only the applicable approved ISR path: in-person signature at the delivery address; signed indirect delivery with the alternate address and door tag recorded; eligible recipient-signed door-tag release; applicable paper SRA; or an electronic signature received in FORGE.
allocation_basis: The cited pages collectively establish all five listed ISR paths without treating them as interchangeable documentation workflows.

claim_text: Complete the path-specific FORGE, signature, address, door-tag, image, and physical-form return prompts; do not substitute ordinary unattended driver release.
allocation_basis: These pages establish the path-specific address, signature, tag, image, scanner, and physical-form handling requirements and exclude generic unattended release.

claim_text: DSR requires an in-person signature from someone at the address on the package label. It cannot be driver released or indirectly delivered.
allocation_basis: All three reviewed sources establish the in-person signer-at-label-address requirement; OP-117 and OP-119 also establish no driver release and no indirect delivery for DSR.

claim_text: A DSR package can be delivered only with an in-person signature from someone at the address on the label. Do not driver release it, use a signed door tag as release authorization, or take it to a neighbor. If nobody can sign, apply the applicable attempt status, complete and scan the door tag, capture the prompted attempt photo, and do not leave the package.
allocation_basis: The sources establish the DSR signer/location and prohibited-release rules; OP-117 and OP-119 establish the unsuccessful-attempt status, door-tag, PPODA, and do-not-leave branch.

claim_text: After three unsuccessful attempts, OP-117 directs the package to QA so the recipient can be contacted. It says another attempt may remain possible, but the reviewed page does not define who authorizes or schedules one.
allocation_basis: OP-117 page 46 establishes QA handoff after three unsuccessful attempts and states that further attempts remain possible without defining authorization or scheduling.

claim_text: Package is identified as Direct Signature Required
allocation_basis: Each source identifies Direct Signature Required as a distinct signature-service branch.

claim_text: The signer must be at the labeled delivery address
allocation_basis: Each source requires the DSR signer to be present at the address on the package label.

allocation_basis: OP-117 page 12 requires an appropriate status code when a signature-service package cannot be delivered.

allocation_basis: OP-117 pages 12, 19, and 34-35 establish door-tag completion/scanning and the prompted PPODA attempt image.

allocation_basis: OP-117 page 46 excludes DSR from the neighbor branch and OP-119 page 13 marks indirect delivery No for DSR.

allocation_basis: OP-117 page 13 and OP-119 page 13 mark Shipment Status Door Tag release No for Direct delivery service.

allocation_basis: OP-117 page 46 establishes QA handoff, recipient contact, and the limited statement that further attempts remain possible.

allocation_basis: The displayed signature type selects the DSR branch.

allocation_basis: Signer presence at the labeled address is the controlling DSR delivery condition.

claim_text: How many unsuccessful attempts have occurred?
allocation_basis: OP-117 page 46 makes the unsuccessful-attempt count relevant to QA handoff.

claim_text: Confirm the package is identified as Direct Signature Required.
allocation_basis: The sources identify DSR as a distinct signature-service branch that must be confirmed before applying its rules.

claim_text: Deliver only after obtaining an in-person signature from someone at the address on the package label.
allocation_basis: All three sources establish in-person signature from someone at the label address as the completed-delivery requirement.

claim_text: If no eligible signer is available, apply the applicable unsuccessful-attempt status, complete and scan the door tag, capture PPODA when prompted, and do not leave the package; retain it for the applicable return or reattempt process.
allocation_basis: OP-117 establishes status, completed/scanned door tag, PPODA prompt, and the unsuccessful branch; OP-119 says the package must not be left when the signature requirement cannot be completed.

claim_text: ASR requires an in-person signature from an eligible recipient who is at least 21 at the package/stop address, is not visibly intoxicated under the FORGE guide, and presents valid government-issued ID for verification. IDs must be checked for every ASR delivery. ASR cannot be driver released or indirectly delivered. Manual date-of-birth entry is allowed only after an ID-scan attempt when a valid ID was presented but scanning was declined or the barcode was unreadable.
allocation_basis: OP-117 pages 12, 14, and 32-33 establish ASR age, address/central-receiving, ID, signature, release, and manual-entry rules; FORGE pages 26 and 92 add the explicit no-visible-intoxication condition.

claim_text: ASR requires an in-person signature from someone 21+ at the delivery address or allowed central receiving area, valid government ID, and no visible intoxication. Attempt the ID scan. Manual DOB entry is allowed only after that attempt when valid ID was presented but scanning was declined or its barcode was unreadable. If no eligible signer or valid ID is available, mark it non-delivered, complete/scan the door tag, capture the prompted attempt photo, and do not leave it. If the recipient refuses to provide ID, use 006, add delivery notation, and return it to the station.
allocation_basis: The cited pages establish eligibility, central receiving, scan/manual/refusal distinctions, the no-signer attempt branch, and do-not-leave requirement.

claim_text: Refusing to provide ID is not the same as declining an ID scan. No ID provided: Status Code 006, delivery notation, and station return. Valid ID presented but scan declined or barcode unreadable after the scan attempt: manual DOB entry and visual-verification attestation are permitted. ASR can never be driver released, indirectly delivered, or released from a signed door tag.
allocation_basis: OP-117 page 33 and OP-119 page 12 distinguish no-ID refusal from declined scanning of presented valid ID; pages 12-13 establish prohibited release methods.

claim_text: Package is identified as Adult Signature Required
allocation_basis: Each source identifies Adult Signature Required as a distinct delivery branch.

claim_text: Recipient is 21 or older
allocation_basis: All cited ASR sources require the signer to be at least 21.

claim_text: Recipient is not visibly intoxicated
allocation_basis: FORGE pages 26 and 92 define an eligible ASR recipient as not visibly intoxicated.

claim_text: Valid government-issued ID is presented
allocation_basis: These sources require government-issued or valid ID presentation/verification for completed ASR delivery.

allocation_basis: OP-117 pages 32-33 and OP-119 page 12 require an ID-scan attempt before manual entry.

allocation_basis: The sources limit manual DOB to presented valid ID followed by declined scanning or an unreadable barcode.

claim_text: At an allowed mailroom or central receiving area within the delivery location, the signer must still be 21 or older, pass the required ID verification, and sign in person
allocation_basis: OP-117 page 14 and OP-119 page 13 allow ASR at an applicable central receiving area only when someone there satisfies the signature and age/ID requirements.

claim_text: Government-issued ID scan or permitted manual date-of-birth/visual-verification record
allocation_basis: These pages define the normal ID scan and the permitted manual DOB/visual-verification record.

claim_text: In-person signature
allocation_basis: Each cited branch requires an in-person signature for completed ASR delivery.

claim_text: When the recipient refuses to provide ID: Status Code 006, delivery notation, and station return
allocation_basis: OP-117 page 33 expressly requires Status Code 006, delivery notation, and station return when ID is refused.

claim_text: When no eligible signer is available: applicable non-delivery status, completed/scanned door tag, and attempt photo when prompted
allocation_basis: OP-117 pages 12 and 34 require an appropriate non-delivery status and completed/scanned door tag when nobody can sign; page 12 and page 34 supply the prompted attempt-photo branch, while FORGE page 94 requires an applicable status for unavailable recipient or invalid ID.

claim_text: No driver release or unattended release
allocation_basis: The cited pages prohibit ASR driver release; FORGE page 92 expressly prohibits unattended release.

claim_text: No indirect delivery
allocation_basis: The cited pages prohibit indirect delivery for ASR.

claim_text: No door-tag signature release
allocation_basis: OP-119 page 13 marks Shipment Status Door Tag release as unavailable for Adult service.

claim_text: Do not use manual DOB entry without first attempting an ID scan
allocation_basis: The sources require an ID-scan attempt before the manual-entry contingency.

claim_text: Do not manually enter DOB unless a valid ID is actually presented and scanning was declined or its barcode was unreadable
allocation_basis: Manual DOB is limited to a presented valid ID whose scan was declined or barcode unreadable.

claim_text: Return the package to the station when the recipient refuses to provide ID. For another unmet ASR requirement, use the applicable non-delivery status/door-tag/PPODA branch and do not leave the package; the reviewed sources do not assign one universal status or disposition to every possible failure condition.
allocation_basis: OP-117 page 33 establishes station return only for refusal to provide ID. The other pages establish applicable non-delivery status, door tag/PPODA, and do-not-leave requirements without assigning one universal status or disposition to every failure.

allocation_basis: The displayed ASR service selects this branch.

allocation_basis: Age and presence at the package/stop address or permitted central receiving area are controlling ASR conditions.

allocation_basis: Valid ID presentation separates completed/manual-verification paths from refusal or invalid-ID non-delivery.

allocation_basis: Scan-attempt state and declined versus unreadable outcome determine whether manual DOB is authorized.

claim_text: Confirm the package is ASR and that delivery is occurring at the labeled/stop address or an allowed mailroom or central receiving area within that delivery location.
allocation_basis: These pages establish the ASR branch and permitted address/central-receiving location scope.

claim_text: Confirm the signer is at least 21 and not visibly intoxicated, inspect the valid government-issued ID, and attempt to scan it in FORGE.
allocation_basis: The sources require eligible age, no visible intoxication under FORGE, valid ID inspection, and an attempted scan.

claim_text: Only if the valid ID barcode is unreadable or the recipient declines scanning after the scan attempt, use Manual entry, enter the exact date of birth from the ID, record the decline when applicable, and select I HAVE VISUALLY VERIFIED AN ID.
allocation_basis: These sources give the complete limited manual DOB, decline-recording, and visual-verification sequence.

claim_text: Confirm the age-verification result, collect the in-person signature, and complete the stop close.
allocation_basis: The sources require age confirmation and an in-person signature after verification.

If no eligible signer is available or the ID/age/signature requirement otherwise cannot be completed, mark the package non-delivered with the applicable status, complete and scan the door tag, capture PPODA when prompted, and do not leave the package.
allocation_basis: OP-117 page 33 gives the exact no-ID refusal branch; the remaining pages give the no-eligible-signer/invalid-ID applicable-status, door-tag, PPODA, and do-not-leave branch.

claim_text: Alcohol cannot be driver released, indirectly delivered, released from a door-tag signature, or delivered to a visibly intoxicated person. Each delivery requires acceptable photo ID regardless of apparent age, age 21 or older, and an in-person adult signature at the labeled address.
allocation_basis: Page 13 establishes alcohol-specific ID, intoxication, and prohibited-release rules; page 32 establishes age 21, in-person signature, and labeled-address requirements.

claim_text: Alcohol requires acceptable photo ID and an in-person adult signature from someone 21+ at the labeled address every time. Do not deliver to a visibly intoxicated person, driver release it, take it to a neighbor, or release it from a signed door tag. If nobody eligible is available, apply the appropriate status, complete and scan the door tag, leave the tag as notice, and do not leave the package.
allocation_basis: Pages 13 and 32 establish the delivery conditions and prohibitions; page 34 establishes status and door-tag steps when nobody can sign; OP-119 page 13 expressly says not to leave the package.

allocation_basis: Page 13 establishes door-tag notice, no release, and penalty warning; pages 32-33 establish the related ID-scan, limited manual-entry, and ID-refusal branches referenced by the answer.

allocation_basis: Page 13 expressly prohibits delivery to a visibly intoxicated person.

allocation_basis: OP-117 page 13 requires the completed/scanned/left alcohol door tag when no adult is available; page 34 supplies the appropriate-status step; OP-119 page 13 says not to leave the package.

claim_text: When individual units are accessible, the attempt is recorded at the unit. If the recipient is unavailable, an eligible neighbor may accept by indirect delivery. If not, a willing apartment office/central receiving/door attendant may accept and sign; OP-117 requires a Status Code 007 and scanned door tag at the unit, followed by the indirect delivery scan and signature at receiving. If nobody will sign, the package is returned after the applicable status and door-tag attempt process.
allocation_basis: The record has one exact evidence fragment, so no competing fragment allocation exists.

claim_text: If the unit is accessible, attempt it there first. For an eligible package, a willing neighbor or office/receiving area may accept and sign. After a failed unit attempt going to the office: apply 007 at the unit, complete/scan a door tag naming the pickup location, leave it on the unit door, then scan the package as Indirect Delivery at the office and get the signature. Never leave it unattended in a common area.
allocation_basis: The record has one exact evidence fragment, so no competing fragment allocation exists.

claim_text: For an otherwise releasable residential package with no safe release location, an eligible indirect delivery may be attempted to a neighbor. The neighbor must sign, the indirect location must be recorded, and a completed/scanned door tag identifying that location must be left at the original recipient's primary entrance. If neither driver release nor eligible indirect delivery is available, apply Status Code 007, complete the matching delivery notation and door-tag/attempt-photo process, and return the package to the station.

claim_text: First confirm the package is eligible for residential driver release. If no secure, protected location exists, do not leave it exposed. If indirect delivery is allowed, enter the neighbor's location, get their signature, and complete/scan a door tag naming that location for the original recipient's front door. If neither option is available, use Status Code 007, add the matching notation, complete/scan the door tag, take the prompted attempt photo, and return the package to the station.
allocation_basis: The current quick reference supplies release eligibility; OP-117 supplies the neighbor, code 007, notation, tag, PPODA, and station-return actions.

claim_text: Do not treat every signature package the same. ISR has a specific indirect-signature path. DSR, ASR, and appointment deliveries cannot use this generic neighbor path. claim_text: Third-party locker delivery is a driver-release service. Only eligible residential packages designated for release without a signature may use it; signature-required, ASR, hazmat, oversize, and commercial packages intended for residential-complex employees are ineligible. If a package does not fit or the locker malfunctions, contact property management for an approved alternate release location, but do not leave the package on, under, near, or on the floor outside the unusable locker. If property management cannot be contacted or no alternate exists, apply Status Code 007 and return the package to the station. Contact the vendor or property management for a wrong-locker delivery. Use only the provided access code and never share it with an unauthorized person.
allocation_basis: Current OP-117 supplies the controlling complete workflow; the portal article corroborates residential/commercial eligibility and property-contact context.

claim_text: OP-117 defines on-duty time broadly from readiness to work until relieved of all work responsibility, including station/shipper waiting, inspection/service, driving, loading/unloading/readiness, disabled-vehicle attendance, specified testing, other motor-carrier work, and compensated outside work. Driving time is all time behind the controls of an operating CMV, including traffic and adverse-road delays. It states an 11-hour driving limit after 10 consecutive hours off, no driving beyond the 14th consecutive hour after coming on duty, no driving after 70 on-duty hours in eight consecutive days, a 34-hour restart option, and a 30-minute break after eight cumulative driving hours unless a qualifying short-haul exception applies.
allocation_basis: The record has one exact evidence fragment, so no competing fragment allocation exists.

OP-117 also says three attempts do not rule out the possibility of further attempts to meet and exceed customer expectations.
allocation_basis: OP-119 page 6 establishes the three-different-Service-Days expectation for packages that cannot be driver released; OP-117 page 46 establishes the QA handoff and further-attempt possibility after three unsuccessful attempts.

claim_text: If the package cannot be driver released, delivery is to be attempted on three different Service Days. After three unsuccessful attempts, give it to QA so the recipient can be contacted. OP-117 says another attempt may still be possible, but the reviewed sources do not say who authorizes or schedules it—ask QA/station before treating a fourth attempt as approved.
allocation_basis: The concise answer combines OP-119's three-Service-Day expectation with OP-117's QA handoff, further-attempt note, and the reviewed-pages authorization limit.

claim_text: OP-119 establishes the three-different-Service-Days attempt expectation for packages that cannot be driver released. allocation_basis: OP-117 page 46 directs the package to QA so the recipient can be contacted after three unsuccessful attempts.
